title: feat: an interactive claude seat exits on a moe END_SESSION handoff so its wrapper relaunches it, instead of idling until a human types /exit
description:
Human-approved 2026-10-26 in the governor REPL (AskUserQuestion "Interactive seats stop and wait for a human /exit whenever the daemon tells them END_SESSION... exit them automatically?" was answered "Yes, auto-exit (Recommended)"). This settles governor-187cc44e's open question #4 from 2026-10-25.

Observed: at 05:37Z architect-4c57a52b called report_blocked on CQ-R09. The reply carried sessionHandoff {action:'END_SESSION', reason:"... Do not call moe.claim_next_task or moe.wait_for_task inside this session ... If this is an interactive TUI, return control to its operator so the CLI can exit normally."}. The architect obeyed, ended its turn ("Exit this CLI session (e.g. /exit ...) to start the next task") and sat idle at the TUI prompt until a human typed /exit at 08:07Z. That was about 2.5 h of planner time lost, with ~25 rows in PLANNING. The daemon emits END_SESSION in reportBlocked.ts (seat freed, no current task) and in claimEligibility.ts blockedHoldGuidance (resource-held task). That is deliberate: commit 43f6dd55 enforces one task per wrapper session, so every task gets a fresh baseline. The gap is only that an interactive TUI cannot end itself.

Direction: scripts/mods/moe-account-switch already turns a moe reply signal (accountSwitch, or claude stopping at the usage limit) into refused claim/wait tools plus a /exit run 10 s after the main turn ends. The wrapper loop then relaunches the seat. Reuse that path for sessionHandoff.action === 'END_SESSION' in any moe tool reply. It is the same mechanism, so this is not a new process. The mod is only loaded for interactive claude seats whose wrapper loop relaunches them (CLAUDE_INTERACTIVE and LOOP_ENABLED; ps1 $claudeInteractive and $loopEnabled), which is exactly the population that needs it. Note that the mod is currently inert without MOE_ACCOUNT_ID. The END_SESSION path should work on an unrotated interactive seat too (it needs only MOE_WORKER_ID), or the task must state why not. Claude seats only; codex/grok TUIs are out of scope.

Ordering: 05e1f916 (DONE) last changed hooks/register.ts. Plan against its landed code.
definitionOfDone: When a moe tool reply in an interactive claude seat whose wrapper loop relaunches it carries sessionHandoff.action END_SESSION (from report_blocked or a held-task claim refusal), the mod runs /exit after the main turn ends, using the existing delayed-exit path. The wrapper relaunches the seat with no human input.

Once END_SESSION has been seen, the mod refuses moe claim_next_task, wait_for_task, chat_wait and start_step for the rest of that session, as it already does for accountSwitch, so no in-session claim breaks the one-task-per-wrapper contract.

No exit is scheduled for headless -p seats, subagent turns, or replies without END_SESSION. The existing accountSwitch and usage-limit paths keep working. The path works on an unrotated interactive seat (no MOE_ACCOUNT_ID), or the task records why it cannot. Any error in the new check leaves the turn and the session as they were (fail open).

scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/hooks/register.test.ts covers the END_SESSION exit, the tool refusal and the no-exit cases. Fresh `claude plugin test scripts/mods/moe-account-switch` passes. The scripts/CLAUDE.md account-switch bullet and docs/MCP_SERVER.md describe the END_SESSION behaviour.
taskRails: Fail open, as the mod does today: an error in the new check must leave the turn and the session as they were.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement END_SESSION on the existing pending/leave/exit path in scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/hooks/register.ts. This design was prototyped at plan time in a scratch copy, and the 26 existing tests stayed green. Keep the file's terse style.
1. Add `const ENDED = 'END-SESSION:'` beside MARK (exporting it is optional), and `const ENDED_FALLBACK = 'End your turn now: Moe relaunches this seat.'`.
2. Move the JSON parse out of switchInstruction into a private replyOf(r). It returns JSON.parse(textOf(r)) for a reply that is neither a deny nor isError, and undefined for an empty text or a failed parse. switchInstruction keeps its exported signature and behaviour: its deny guard and its start_step isError branch still run first, and only then does its top-level accountSwitch read go through replyOf.
3. Add an exported endSessionInstruction(r, workerId). It reads replyOf(r)?.sessionHandoff at TOP LEVEL only, because a chat message quoting a handoff sits under messages[]. It returns `${ENDED} ${reason}` only when the handoff's action === 'END_SESSION' and its workerId === workerId, the seat's own MOE_WORKER_ID. A handoff the daemon addressed to another seat must not end this session, for example after a caller named the assignee's workerId. reason is the handoff's reason, trimmed, when that is a non-blank string, else ENDED_FALLBACK. Anything else returns undefined: null, a string, an array, a missing field.
4. tool.call: for a moe tool, read MOE_WORKER_ID first; when it is unset or empty, return next(e) untouched. Keep the HELD refusal and the main-turn abort exactly as they are: they now serve END_SESSION too. Then read MOE_ACCOUNT_ID as leased. Only a leased seat gets acceptsAccountSwitch on MARKED calls and has switchInstruction consulted (`if (leased) session.pending ??= switchInstruction(tool, r)`), so account behaviour is unchanged. Then, only while nothing is pending, compute endSessionInstruction(r, workerId). When it returns an instruction, await $.session.surfaces() and set `session.pending ??= instruction` only if the list is non-empty. A -p run draws on no surface and ends with its turn anyway, so the mod never refuses or exits there; the wrapper never loads the mod there either. Keep `.catch(($, e, next) => next(e))`. It is replay-safe: a throw anywhere in the new check (an env read, the parse, surfaces) hands back the daemon's reply untouched, calls nothing twice and sets nothing. That is the fail-open error handling the task rail requires.
5. checkHardLimit and classic.StopFailure stay gated on isSeat (both variables), unchanged. checkHardLimit already returns early while anything is pending.
6. leave() and exit() name the kind: `const ended = session.pending.startsWith(ENDED)`. For END_SESSION, leave() toasts 'Moe: this task session is over. This session ends in 10 s and Moe relaunches it.'; otherwise it shows the existing account text, unchanged. It schedules exit($, ended) on the same EXIT_DELAY_MS timer, behind the same once-only exiting latch. exit()'s catch toasts 'Moe: this task session is over. Type /exit and Moe relaunches it.' for END_SESSION, else the existing account fallback, unchanged. The first signal of a session wins (??=), as it does today.
7. Rewrite the header comment to cover both triggers. The mod also ends the session on the daemon's END_SESSION handoff: report_blocked freeing the seat, or a claim_next_task/wait_for_task refusal over a resource-held task. It does this because a TUI cannot end itself, and the next task needs a fresh wrapper pre-flight. The account switch needs a leased seat (MOE_WORKER_ID and MOE_ACCOUNT_ID); END_SESSION needs only MOE_WORKER_ID and a session that draws on a surface. The mod fails open.
8. scripts/mods/moe-account-switch/.claude-plugin/plugin.json: change only description, for example 'Ends an interactive Moe seat's session at a turn boundary when Moe says its Claude account is spent or hands it an END_SESSION, so the wrapper relaunches it.' name and version stay, because the wrappers find the mod by its folder name.
Do not edit scripts/moe-agent.sh or scripts/moe-agent.ps1. They already load the mod into every interactive claude seat whose loop relaunches it, leased or not (scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs pins this), and any wrapper edit hot-reloads every running seat. Re-run the step-4 test command: every test is green.
implementationPlan.note:
Green. Changes to register.ts:
- Added ENDED='END-SESSION:' (exported) and ENDED_FALLBACK.
- Added a private replyOf(r): undefined for a deny, isError, empty text or failed parse.
- switchInstruction keeps its deny guard and start_step isError branch first, then reads accountSwitch through replyOf; its behaviour is unchanged.
- Added exported endSessionInstruction(r, workerId): top-level sessionHandoff only, object only, action==='END_SESSION' and workerId===MOE_WORKER_ID; reason trimmed, else the fallback.
- tool.call: MOE_WORKER_ID gates it; the HELD refusal and abort are unchanged; `leased` = MOE_ACCOUNT_ID gates acceptsAccountSwitch and switchInstruction; END_SESSION is read only while nothing is pending, and only with a non-empty $.session.surfaces(); `.catch(next)` is kept.
- leave()/exit(ended) pick the END_SESSION toast and fallback by prefix.
- Header comment rewritten. checkHardLimit and StopFailure are unchanged (isSeat).

plugin.json: description only.

register.test.ts fix: the IGNORED cases are now [tool, reply] tuples, so `Object.keys()[0]` no longer trips noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

Keep the project's global forbiddenPatterns out of every text you write.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of `git diff` over the six files. No code changes were needed.
- Concurrency: the first signal wins through `??=` in tool.call and checkHardLimit. END_SESSION is computed only while nothing is pending, and a race during the surfaces await still keeps the first value (`??=`). The once-only `exiting` latch in leave() means two END_SESSION replies, or END_SESSION plus a usage-limit completion, schedule one exit (the existing order/concurrency tests cover the latch).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: reuse moe-account-switch's pending/leave/exit path, as the task directs. It is the only mod both wrappers load into exactly the interactive+loop claude population, and it already turns a moe reply signal into four refused tools plus a delayed /exit. Rejected:
(1) A new mod. It would duplicate the exit machinery and need a second plugin dir in both wrappers, and a wrapper edit hot-reloads every running seat.
(2) A daemon-side change. The daemon never runs or kills a CLI; the wrapper owns the process lifecycle.
(3) Keeping END_SESSION behind MOE_ACCOUNT_ID. The DoD wants unrotated seats covered, and the wrapper already loads the mod without a lease.
(4) Relying only on wrapper gating for -p. Instead, a $.session.surfaces() check (an empty list means a -p or SDK run) lets register.test.ts prove the -p case itself, while prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs still pins the wrapper half. The check applies only to the new path, so the shipped account and usage-limit paths keep their behaviour.
(5) Honouring any END_SESSION. A handoff addressed to another seat (sessionHandoff.workerId is the assignee's) must not end this one, so its workerId must equal MOE_WORKER_ID.
(6) A new Session field for the kind. An 'END-SESSION:' prefix on the pending instruction mirrors MARK and keeps one string.
(7) Updating the wrapper comments about the mod. Skipped: the hot-reload hazard, and they stay true for the account switch.
Docs scope: the two files the DoD names, plus docs/CONFIGURATION.md (the opt-out now also turns off the END_SESSION exit) and plugin.json's description. The docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md account-switch entry stays accurate, and the END_SESSION toast explains itself. The plan touches 6 distinct files, so the daemon's soft warning (>5) is expected: two are code, about 200 test lines and about 15 doc lines.

completionSummary:
An interactive claude seat whose wrapper loop relaunches it now ends its session on the daemon's END_SESSION handoff. It uses the existing moe-account-switch path: the pending instruction, the refusal of claim_next_task/wait_for_task/chat_wait/start_step with the main turn aborted, and /exit 10 s after the main turn ends.

register.ts:
- endSessionInstruction(r, workerId) reads a top-level sessionHandoff from a successful reply, only when action==='END_SESSION' and workerId===MOE_WORKER_ID. The reason is trimmed, else 'End your turn now: Moe relaunches this seat.'
- It needs only MOE_WORKER_ID, so it works on an unrotated seat. MOE_ACCOUNT_ID still gates acceptsAccountSwitch and switchInstruction.
- It requires a non-empty $.session.surfaces(), so it never acts in a -p run.
- The first signal wins (??=). The toasts and the failed-/exit fallback name the kind.
- It fails open through the replay-safe .catch(next).
- checkHardLimit and StopFailure are unchanged.
